title: Implicitly nullable parameter types are deprecated
summary: PHP 8.4 deprecates giving a typed parameter a default value of null without also marking the type itself nullable ("?Type" or "Type|null"); the parameter still accepts null, but omitting the explicit nullable marker now raises a deprecation notice.
new_code_policy: Never write a typed parameter's nullability implicitly through a "= null" default; write it in the type itself, e.g. "function f(?int $x = null)" or "function f(int|null $x = null)", including for constructor-promoted parameters.
existing_code_policy: Add the missing "?"/"|null" to each declaration as E_DEPRECATED notices surface. This only makes the parameter's existing nullability explicit in its type; it does not change what values the parameter accepts or how the function body behaves, so it is safe to apply broadly rather than case by case.
guideline: Always spell a nullable parameter type explicitly ("?Type" or "Type|null") instead of relying on a "null" default to make an otherwise non-nullable type implicitly nullable.
details: Since long before PHP 8, a scalar, class, or compound parameter type followed by a default value of exactly null (e.g. "function f(int $x = null)") has been silently treated as if the type were nullable ("?int $x = null"), even though the "?" was never written. PHP 8.4 deprecates that implicit behavior: the parameter is still nullable and the default is still null, but the declaration itself must now say so, or an E_DEPRECATED notice fires (RFC deprecate-implicitly-nullable-types). This applies to ordinary and constructor-promoted parameters alike, and only to declarations whose default value is literally null; it does not apply to "mixed" (already nullable), to a union type that already lists null explicitly, or to properties or return types, which this deprecation does not cover. No later UPGRADING file records an escalation to removal: the one PHP 8.5 UPGRADING hit for "nullable" is an unrelated change to SplFileObject::fwrite(), so as of 8.5 this remains a deprecation notice only.
notes: The rewrite is purely additive to the type declaration (adding "?" or "|null"); it changes no runtime behavior, so it can be applied mechanically to every occurrence rather than needing case-by-case judgment.

Only a default value of exactly null triggers this; "mixed $x = null" is unaffected because "mixed" already includes null, and a union type that already spells out "|null" is unaffected because the nullability is already explicit.

Evidence: UPGRADING-8.4.0.txt, '4. Deprecated Functionality' -> Core: "Implicitly nullable parameter types are now deprecated." (RFC deprecate-implicitly-nullable-types). Grepping the 8.5 UPGRADING file for "nullable" found only an unrelated SplFileObject::fwrite() change, and no PHP 8.2, 8.3 or 8.5 UPGRADING file records a removal, so this remains a deprecation-only fact as of PHP 8.5.
